item.description:

item.title: APSI Summer Book Club 2026: To Save and to Destroy — Mon Aug 17, 9:00 AM — Online
item.description:
APSI's summer book club is back by popular demand. This year, the books have been chosen to set the stage for APSI's annual keynote talk (November 2026) which will feature author and professor Viet Thanh Nguyen.
Professor Eileen Cheng-yin Chow (Duke) concludes our two-book sequence with Nguyen's newest book, To Save and to Destroy, which was shortlisted for the National Book Critics Circle Award in Criticism.
The discussion will take place online, so members of the community near and far are welcome to join.
Be sure to register via Zoom (https://duke.zoom.us/meeting/register/0zQgAwqnRFai8lhl1I8x-g)
From the publisher The essays here, delivered originally as the prestigious Norton Lectures, proffer a new answer to a classic literary question: What does the outsider mean to literary writing? Over the course of six captivating and moving chapters, Nguyen explores the idea of being an outsider through lenses that are, by turns, literary, historical, political, and familial.

item.title: Graduate Summer School in Stochastics, Dynamics, and Machine Learning — Mon Aug 17, 9:00 AM — Gross Hall 103
item.description:
This graduate summer school will feature five speakers, each giving multiple tutorial lectures to introduce current topics in the area of stochastic dynamics and connections with machine learning. The target audience is graduate students and postdocs in mathematics, working in this broad research area. There will also be a poster session and problem sessions related to the lectures. Speakers are: Alex Blumenthal, Jianfeng Lu, Kavita Ramanan, Maximilian Engel, Ricardo Baptista. For more details, including the schedule, visit the website: https://sites.duke.edu/stochasticdynamics26/
Source: Duke University

item.title: Mobile Health Assessment — Mon Aug 17, 10:00 AM — None
item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Additionally, there is a goal setting and referral session with a nurse, dietitian, or fitness specialist. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Patch-a-Palooza at Vance Birthplace — Sat Sep 19, 10:00 AM — Governor Zebulon B. Vance Birthplace
item.description:
Join us on Saturday, September 19th for a day of sensory learning and fun at Vance Birthplace! Patch-a-Palooza welcomes families with K-8th grade children to try their hands at various historic activities from writing with a quill pen to playing historic games. Each learning station has a stamp, and children who earn a stamp from every station will receive a Vance Birthplace patch along with their take-home crafts. This is a great opportunity for children to learn about life in Western North Carolina in the 1800s while working on their fine motor, artistic, and critical thinking skills.
Admission is $7 per child to cover the cost of craft supplies. Adults may enter for free unless they choose to participate in the crafts. Enter through the visitor center to pay admission and receive stamp cards. This event is appropriate for all ages but is primarily geared toward elementary and middle grade learners.
For more information, email us at vance@dncr.nc.gov or give us a call at (828) 645-

Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. item.title: DEADLINE: America 250 NC Corn Maze Competition — Thu Oct 1
item.description:
Who has the most ah-MAZE-ing America 250 design?
Competition Details
Do you have a corn maze? Are you planning an America 250-themed design? We want to hear from you!
Details: Please send us a photo of your corn maze, with your name and location, to America250NC@dncr.nc.gov. After the deadline, our team will vote in office for our favorite design! All photos will be posted on our website and social media to celebrate your creativity.
Prize: Exclusive prize pack and a visit from the America 250 NC team to your maze! Can we escape? Details of our visit will go on our social media pages.
Deadline: October 1, 2026
Corn maze must be in North Carolina to be eligible. All entries must be by adults 18 or older. Entry is not a guarantee of a visit or prize.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Latinos & Latinas Run Club — Thu Aug 13, 6:30 PM — The Glass Jug Downtown
item.description:
Come connect with us over a run! Hosted by Latinos Run and Latinas Run of Raleigh & Durham, all paces and people are welcome weekly starting at 6:30pm. We’ll follow a 3–4 mile route through downtown Durham before returning to us here at Glass Jug Downtown for drinks and camaraderie. Latinos Run and Latinas Run are nationwide running organizations dedicated to empowering and connecting communities through running, wellness, and culture. Their mission is to create a supportive, inclusive space where individuals of all backgrounds and fitness levels feel welcomed and encouraged to move their bodies and build meaningful connections. You can learn more about the organizations here: https://www.latinosrun.com/ We aim to be a welcoming space for runners to connect, move, and enjoy each other’s company – so join us, Latinos Run, and Latinas Run every Thursday!

item.description:
Clyde and Catherine Edgerton will delight us with a concert of old traditional tunes and stories based upon his family growing up in what is now William B. Umstead State Park.
Clyde Edgerton's family grew up on what is now William B. Umstead State Park. Clyde is well know as a North Carolina author and professor; Catherine a singer, guitarist, and artist.
Light refreshments will be served. Come see the status of our restoration of the 1937 Sycamore Mess Hall.
Parking: Sycamore Multi-use Trail head, gravel parking lot. Enter Park from US70/Glenwood Ave (Crabtree) entrance. (allow 20 minutes drive from Park entrance)
Concert 6pm; Doors open 5pm

Our TRACK Trail is located on the Holly Discovery Trail as you enter Lake James State Park-Paddy's Creek Access. The parking lot, is the first parking lot on the left after you cross the entrance bridge on Lake James State Park Road. After you park, walk over to the TRACK Trails Kiosk to grab an activity brochure to complete as you hike the Holly Discovery Trail. Once you complete the hike and activity brochure, take the completed brochure to the visitor center to receive custom TRACK Trails Prizes. item.title: Aging Gracefully Creative Movement Workshop — Wed Aug 19, 11:00 AM — Arts Together
item.description:
Ages 50+ Aging Gracefully: Meaningful Movement Explorations – As we age it is important to keep the body moving, the brain focused, and the spirit fueled. In this technique/creative dance class, we will do so in a healthy, FUN way. We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. Inspired by poetry, visual art, and personal experience, we will create dances; accessing the wisdom of the body to express our relationship to the world, each other, and ourselves. No prior dance experience needed, just a willing heart <3

item.title: Whack Attack Invasive Plant Removal Workday — Wed Sep 9, 9:30 AM — Lower Haw River State Natural Area
item.description: Friends of Lower Haw is having an invasive plant removal workday with NC State Parks biologists on September 9th from 9:30 am until 3:00 pm, or whenever you need to leave. Meeting location is the parking lot at 4551 US Hwy 15-501 N, Pittsboro. Meet in the parking lot at 9:30 am and stay however long you want to help. We will be working in the Pegg Tract area of the Lower Haw River State Natural Area, located upstream of the Bynum Dam by US Hwy 15-501. Invasive plant workdays involve identifying and removing non-native plants using clippers, pruners, saws, and other non-motorized hand tools. Learn about invasive plants and removal techniques. Hand tools will be available, or volunteers can bring their own loppers or hand pruners. Bring your own work gloves, insect repellent, and drinking water. item.title: Sunrise Fall Walk — Wed Sep 23, 6:30 AM — Mayo River Bridge Kayak Launch
item.description:
Join us at Mayo River State Park for a Sunrise FallWalk!
Enjoy the beginning of the fall season with the morning sunrise, where we will be walking along the unmarked Mayo Meadows Trail. An easy out-and-back walk that takes no more than an hour, along dirt and grass through large fields. Please bring flashlight as the trailhead will be very dark when we being. Cameras and binoculars are encouraged.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather. Please click the "I'm Interested" button as event will cancel when there are no registrations and recieve emails if canceled due to weather.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Harvest Moon Hike — Sat Sep 26, 8:00 PM — Mayo River State Park
item.description:
Join us at Mayo River State Park for a Harvest Moon Hike!
The Harvest Moon is the full moon of the Fall Equinox and named after the peak harvesting season for farmers, as the brightness would extend the harvesting days. We encourage you to come join us in celebration of the beginning of the fall season as we hike along the Fox Trail, an easy-moderate 2 mile hike, through the peaceful foliage of the Mayo Mountain area.
Please bring water, hiking shoes, and flashlights.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather. Please click the "I'm Interested" button as event will cancel when there are no registrations and recieve emails if canceled due to weather.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Overmountain Victory Trail Celebration — Wed Sep 30, 4:00 PM — Fonta Flora Brewery at Whippoorwill Farm
item.description:
Join us for this FREE event as we celebrate the Annual Overmountain Victory Men March—no actual marching required! Step back in time and experience the sights, sounds, and stories of the Revolutionary War as we honor the remarkable journey of the Overmountain Victory Men and their role in changing the course of American history.
Enjoy live music, delicious food, a photo booth, guided hikes, living history demonstrations, local history exhibits, and hands-on activities for all ages. Discover how people lived, traveled, and survived along the historic Overmountain Victory Trail while exploring the traditions and heritage of the Appalachian frontier.
Whether you're a history enthusiast, outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a fun family outing, there's something for everyone!
Source: NC Cultural Resources
